answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond locked in a public contract: each identity posts collateral, and any participant can submit evidence that it double-signs a task or breaks a stated rule. A successful challenge burns part of the bond and rewards the challenger. Creating sybils therefore requires funding each one, while coordinating them risks losing capital; the karst network may offer a haven for newcomers, but their weight still grows only as they post bonds, with penalties flowing through the delta.
